extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics (readers of Kant)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and analytic moments for forming and evaluating aesthetic judgements of the Beautiful and the Sublime, with distinctions between pure taste, purposiveness without purpose, and the mathematically vs dynamically sublime. Intended as guidance for philosophical analysis of aesthetic experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgement of taste claims a subjective necessity grounded in a common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition of necessity which a judgement of taste asserts is the Idea of a common sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgements of taste have a subjective principle (feeling) that nonetheless lays claim to universal validity; this common sense is different from the Understanding's 'common sense' (sensus communis) because it judges by feeling rather than concepts. The assumption of a common sense allows the subject to demand universal assent for a taste-judgement, provided the case is correctly subsumed under that ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for presupposing a common sense: universal communicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitions and judgements must, along with the conviction that accompanies them, admit of universal communicability; otherwise there would be no harmony between them and the Object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the accordance of cognitive powers (Imagination exciting Understanding to unity) must admit of universal communicability, and since the universal communicability of a feeling presupposes a common sense, we have grounds to assume a common sense as the necessary condition of the universal communicability of our knowledge (used as a presupposition rather than a psychological claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective necessity represented as objective under presupposition of common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity of the universal agreement thought in a judgement of taste is a subjective necessity, which is represented as objective under the presupposition of a common sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When we describe anything as beautiful we refuse to allow another opinion, not because the judgement is grounded on concepts but because we place feeling at its basis as a communal feeling. This communal feeling is an ideal norm: it says not that everyone will agree, but that they ought to; thus the principle is subjective yet assumed as subjectively universal and can claim universal assent provided correct subsumption under it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty defined: object of a necessary satisfaction without concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The beautiful is that which without any concept is cognised as the object of a necessary satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judgement of the beautiful does not arise from concepts nor from the object's utility; instead it is a necessary satisfaction felt when the Imagination's free conformity to the law of the Understanding is experienced. The judgement claims universal validity even though it is grounded in feeling and not conceptual cognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposiveness without purpose (free conformity to law) as necessary for taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste is a faculty for judging an object in reference to the Imagination’s free conformity to law — bringing about autonomy with the Imagination of itself conformed to law (purposiveness without purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a pure judgement of taste the Imagination must be considered in its freedom (productive, spontaneous), yet its product must accord with the norm-like law of the Understanding. If imagination's product is determined by definite concepts, the satisfaction becomes that of the Good (formal perfection) rather than the Beautiful. Thus beauty requires free play of imagination in sensible presentation while remaining in harmony with understanding (no conceptual determination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purity of taste: no reference to use or practical purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure judgement of taste combines satisfaction or dissatisfaction without any reference to its use or to a purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When taste is pure it is disinterested: approval is not tied to the object's availability for designs or practical applications. If the object's regularity is judged with respect to purpose or cognition (e.g., utility, intelligibility), the satisfaction belongs to the Good or the merely agreeable, not the Beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness / 'devoid of interest' as a moment of aesthetical judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the analysis of the aesthetical judgement the satisfaction must be represented according to quality as devoid of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic judgement's quality is that it provides pleasure independent of desire or practical interest (disinterested). This is part of the fourfold analytic moments applied to both beauty and the sublime (quantity, quality, relation, modality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to rigid mathematical regularity; novelty and free play preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: All stiff regularity (such as approximates to mathematical regularity) has something in it repugnant to taste; the imagination prefers objects with which it can play in an unstudied and purposive manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularity that prescribes a definite concept for the object tends toward cognition or practical use and produces weariness when repeated; conversely, form that allows free imaginative play (even near the grotesque) sustains taste. Examples: geometric figures often satisfy understanding but not pure taste; English gardens and bizarre furniture may display freedom that pleases taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Beautiful and Sublime (form vs formlessness; quality vs quantity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beautiful in nature is connected with the form of the object, which consists in having boundaries. The Sublime is to be found in a formless object, so far as in it or by occasion of it boundlessness is represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty relates to the presentation of an indefinite concept of Understanding (quality) and leads to pleasurable play of Imagination. The Sublime concerns Ideas of Reason (quantity, boundlessness) and produces pleasure only indirectly — a feeling of being checked then renewed, giving admiration or respect (negative pleasure). Thus the two require different kinds of aesthetic response and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime involves a movement of mind and is either mathematical or dynamical
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of the Sublime brings with it as its characteristic feature a movement of the mind bound up with the judging of the object, and the analysis divides the sublime into the mathematically and the dynamically sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the sublime involves a dynamic response (movement rather than restful contemplation), the representation is referred through Imagination either to the faculty of cognition (mathematical) or to that of desire (dynamical). Mathematical sublime pertains to magnitude and comprehension; dynamical sublime pertains to might or power and the relation to our physical/mental powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematically sublime: absolute greatness beyond comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: We call that sublime which is absolutely great. The sublime is that which, the mere ability to think which, shows a faculty of the mind surpassing every standard of Sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mathematically sublime arises when the mind encounters magnitude that cannot be adequately comprehended in intuition (comprehensio aesthetica reaches its maximum). It is not the object's sensory size per se that is sublime but the state of mind produced — the imagination's inadequacy and Reason's demand for totality, which produces the feeling of a supersensible faculty. Examples: very large natural objects whose magnitude overwhelms imagination (Pyramids, vast spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic (intuitive) estimation of magnitude vs mathematical measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The estimation of magnitude by mere intuition (by the measurement of the eye) is aesthetical; mathematical estimation uses concepts of number — aesthetic estimation can reach a subjective maximum that yields the idea of the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical/logical measures proceed by number and can extend to infinity; aesthetic apprehension involves apprehensio and comprehensio aesthetica. Comprehension reaches a limit beyond which imagination cannot present the whole: this limit is the source of the feeling of the mathematically sublime. Practical implication: vantage (distance) matters — too close or too far reduces the sublime effect (e.g., Pyramids, St. Peter's).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure aesthetic judgement of the sublime must avoid artefacts and teleological construals
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure judgement upon the sublime must have no purpose of the Object as its determining ground, if it is to be aesthetical and not mixed up with any judgement of Understanding or Reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exhibit the sublime in products of art (where human purpose determines form and size) nor in natural things whose concepts bring a definite purpose (animals with known natural ends). For pure sublime, present rude nature merely as containing magnitude (not monstrous, which would destroy the object's concept).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime produces a negative pleasure (admiration/respect) via momentary checking then stronger outflow of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of the Sublime is a pleasure that arises only indirectly; it is produced by the feeling of a momentary checking of the vital powers and a consequent stronger outflow of them, so that it seems to be regarded as emotion — earnest in the exercise of the Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike the Beautiful (restful contemplation), the Sublime alternately repels and attracts, producing admiration or respect rather than mere charm. This explains why objects that violently exceed our faculties can yet be experienced as sublime (so long as they do not invoke mere horror or practical danger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptual conditions affect experience of the sublime (apprehension/comprehension limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: In receiving a quantum into the Imagination by intuition there are two operations: apprehension and comprehension; comprehension becomes harder as apprehension advances and soon attains a maximum — the aesthetically greatest fundamental measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: to experience the full emotional effect of magnitude one needs an optimal distance and vantage point (e.g., not too near/far from the Pyramids or St. Peter’s). If too far parts are obscure; if too near comprehension of the whole is impossible, reducing the sublime effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime is not in sense-objects but in the mind's representation and its relation to Ideas of Reason
rubrics_metrics.description: No sensible form can contain the sublime properly so-called. The sublime is found only in our Ideas, and it is the state of mind produced by a certain representation with which the reflective Judgement is occupied that is to be called sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects of nature may occasion the feeling of sublimity (when they suggest boundlessness or might), but the proper locus of the sublime is the mind's recognition of faculties (Imagination vs Reason) and the Idea of the infinite or absolute totality; e.g., a stormy ocean may be horrible rather than sublime unless it calls to higher Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic moments for aesthetical judgement (applied to sublime and beautiful)
rubrics_metrics.description: The satisfaction in the Sublime (as with the Beautiful) must be represented according to quantity (universally valid), quality (devoid of interest), relation (subjective purposiveness), and modality (necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four analytic moments when analysing aesthetic judgements: start with quantity for the sublime (because of formlessness and boundlessness), unlike the beautiful where quality was first investigated. This provides a methodical way to assess aesthetic claims of universal validity and necessity.
